misconceptions.believed: The S040 documentation-only journal accurately described the state that reached the repository
misconceptions.revealed_by: The working tree carried runner/term/_process/_windows_job code, tests, and an IN FLIGHT T8 trajectory, none of which S040 recorded; the first commit paired a docs-only journal with an implementation diff
misconceptions.corrected_to: Discovery (S040) and implementation (S041) are separate sessions; data/ records are immutable (N6), so S040 stands unedited and S041 is added
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: A journal entry must describe the diff it ships in; a discovery record cannot ride along with implementation code.

misconceptions.believed: `python3 -m unittest discover` reproduces the recorded op-count baselines on any host
misconceptions.revealed_by: This host's python3 is 3.14.7 and produced 25 failures; python3.11 (3.11.15, the baseline interpreter) is clean
misconceptions.corrected_to: Op counts are interpreter-version-dependent; the baselines are pinned to CPython 3.11 and the gates must be invoked as python3.11 here
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: A reproducibility baseline is only reproducible against the interpreter that produced it; pin the interpreter, not just the sandbox backend.

decisions.decision: Record the implementation as a new session S041 rather than editing S040
alternatives: Squash discovery and implementation into one record
decisions.rationale: data/ is immutable (N6) and S040 is truthful about the discovery phase, so the fix is additive, not corrective

decisions.decision: Drain child pipes with reader threads and a bounded queue instead of select()
decisions.rationale: Windows cannot select() on anonymous pipes; threads work on every OS, drain stderr concurrently, bound memory, and keep run_code's signature stable

friction.description: The implementation transcript ended on a failing portability test; the committed tree has all 17 green
